q.t: Find the volume of a cube of side 4 cm.
q.e: Volume = side × side × side.

q.t: Find the volume of a cylinder of radius 7 cm and height 10 cm. (π = 22/7)
q.e: Base area × height: 154 × 10.

q.t: Find the volume of a cone of radius 7 cm and height 12 cm. (π = 22/7)
q.e: A cone holds ⅓ of the cylinder on the same base and height: ⅓ × 154 × 12.

q.t: Find the volume of a sphere of radius 21 cm. (π = 22/7)
Find the curved surface area of a cylinder of radius 7 cm and height 10 cm. (π = 22/7)
q.e: Unroll it into a rectangle: circumference 44 × height 10.

q.t: A cone has radius 6 cm and height 8 cm. Find its slant height.
q.e: Radius, height and slant height make a right triangle: √(36 + 64).

q.t: Find the surface area of a sphere of radius 7 cm. (π = 22/7)
q.e: S = 4πr² — four times the area of its biggest circle.

q.t: Find the volume of a 5 cm × 4 cm × 3 cm cuboid.
q.e: length × breadth × height.

q.t: Find the total surface area of a solid hemisphere of radius 7 cm. (π = 22/7)
q.e: Curved part 2πr² plus the flat circle πr²: 3πr².

q.t: Find the curved surface area of a cone of radius 7 cm and slant height 10 cm. (π = 22/7)
A toy is a cone of radius 7 cm and height 24 cm on a hemisphere of the same radius. Find its total surface area. (π = 22/7)
q.e: Slant height = 25. Outside surface = cone’s πrl + hemisphere’s 2πr² = 550 + 308.

q.t: A cylinder and a cone have the same base and height. Find volume of cylinder : volume of cone.
q.e: A cone holds exactly one-third of the matching cylinder.

q.t: Two cubes of volume 64 cm³ each are joined end to end. Find the surface area of the cuboid.
q.e: Each cube has side 4, so the cuboid is 8 × 4 × 4: 2(32 + 32 + 16).

q.t: A hemispherical bowl has radius 10.5 cm. Find its inner curved surface area. (π = 22/7)
A well of diameter 7 m is dug 20 m deep. Find the volume of earth taken out. (π = 22/7)
q.e: It is a cylinder: 22/7 × 3.5² × 20.

q.t: Two spheres have radii in the ratio 2 : 3. Find the ratio of their volumes.
q.e: Volume goes with r³.

q.t: A cylinder of radius 7 cm and height 10 cm has a hemisphere of radius 7 cm on top. Find the curved surface area of the whole solid (leave out the flat base). (π = 22/7)
q.e: The outside is the cylinder's curved side, 2πrh = 440, plus the hemisphere's curved surface, 2πr² = 308. The flat top of the cylinder is covered by the hemisphere, so it is not counted. 440 + 308 = 748.

q.t: A cone has radius 3.5 cm and height 12 cm. Find its slant height.
q.e: Height, radius and slant height form a right triangle, so l = √(3.5² + 12²) = √(12.25 + 144) = √156.25 = 12.5.

q.t: Find the volume of a hemisphere of radius 21 cm. (π = 22/7)
q.e: A hemisphere is half a sphere: ½ × (4/3)πr³ = (2/3)πr³ = 2/3 × 22/7 × 9261 = 19404.

q.t: A toy is a cone standing on a hemisphere of the same radius, 3.5 cm. The toy is 15.5 cm tall. How tall is the cone?
q.e: The hemisphere's height is its radius, 3.5 cm. The rest of the height is the cone: 15.5 − 3.5 = 12.

q.t: A capsule is a cylinder with a hemisphere at each end. It is 20 cm long with diameter 6 cm. Find its surface area. (π = 22/7)
q.e: The cylinder part is 20 − 6 = 14 long. 2π × 3 × 14 + 4π × 9 = 120π.

q.t: A cone of the same radius (7 cm) and height (24 cm) is hollowed out of a solid cylinder. Find the volume left. (π = 22/7)
q.e: Cylinder 3696 minus cone ⅓ of it: ⅔ × 3696.

q.t: How many litres does a 4 m × 3 m × 2 m tank hold?
q.e: 24 m³, and 1 m³ = 1000 L.

q.t: A cube of side 7 cm has a hemisphere of diameter 7 cm stuck on top. Find the total surface area. (π = 22/7)
q.e: Cube faces 6 × 49 = 294. The hemisphere hides a circle πr² of the top face but adds its curved surface 2πr². Net change +πr² = 22/7 × 12.25 = 38.5. Total 332.5.

q.t: A toy is a cone (radius 3.5 cm, height 12 cm) on a hemisphere of the same radius. Find its total surface area. (π = 22/7)
q.e: Only the curved parts show. Cone: slant height √(3.5² + 12²) = 12.5, so πrl = 137.5. Hemisphere: 2πr² = 77. Total 214.5.

q.t: The same toy (cone of radius 3.5 cm and height 12 cm on a hemisphere of radius 3.5 cm). Find its volume. (π = 22/7)
q.e: Volumes simply add. Cone (1/3)πr²h = 154. Hemisphere (2/3)πr³ = 539/6. Total 154 + 539/6 = 1463/6.

q.t: A capsule is a cylinder with a hemisphere at each end. It is 21 cm long and its radius is 3.5 cm. Find its volume. (π = 22/7)
q.e: The two hemispheres take 3.5 cm each, so the cylinder is 21 − 7 = 14 cm long: πr²h = 539. The two hemispheres make one sphere: (4/3)πr³ = 539/3. Total 2156/3.

q.t: A solid is a hemisphere of radius 7 cm with a cone of the same radius on top. The cone's height equals its radius. Find the volume. (π = 22/7)
q.e: Hemisphere (2/3)πr³ plus cone (1/3)πr² × r = (1/3)πr³. Together exactly πr³ = 22/7 × 343 = 1078.

q.t: A pen stand is a 15 cm × 10 cm × 3.5 cm block of wood with four conical holes, each of radius 0.5 cm and depth 1.4 cm. Find the volume of wood left. (π = 22/7)
A cylinder of height 10 cm and radius 3.5 cm has a hemisphere scooped out of each end. Find the total surface area. (π = 22/7)
q.e: The outside is the curved side 2πrh = 220 plus the inside of two hollow hemispheres, 2 × 2πr² = 154. The flat ends are gone. Total 374.

q.t: A tent is a cylinder of radius 7 m and height 3 m with a cone of slant height 10 m on top. Canvas costs ₹50 per m². Find the cost of canvas (in ₹). (π = 22/7)
A solid is a cylinder of radius 7 cm and height 10 cm topped by a hemisphere of radius 7 cm. Find its volume. (π = 22/7)
q.e: Cylinder 1540 + hemisphere (2/3) × 22/7 × 343 = 2156/3.

q.t: A solid hemisphere has total surface area 462 cm². Find its volume. (π = 22/7)
A glass vessel is a sphere of diameter 8.5 cm with a cylindrical neck 8 cm long and 2 cm across. About how much water does it hold? (π = 3.14)
q.e: Sphere (4/3)πr³ with r = 4.25: about 321.39. Neck πr²h with r = 1, h = 8: 25.12. Total about 346.51 cm³.

q.t: A cone of the same height (2.4 cm) and diameter (1.4 cm) is hollowed out of a solid cylinder. Find the total surface area of what is left. (π = 22/7)
q.e: What shows: the cylinder's side 2πrh = 10.56, its bottom circle πr² = 1.54, and the inside of the cone πrl, where l = √(0.7² + 2.4²) = 2.5, so 5.5. The top circle is gone. Total 17.6.

q.t: A medicine capsule is a cylinder with a hemisphere at each end. It is 14 mm long and 5 mm across. Find its surface area. (π = 22/7)
q.e: r = 2.5, and the cylinder part is 14 − 5 = 9 mm long: 2πrh = 990/7. The two hemispheres make a sphere: 4πr² = 550/7. Total 1540/7 = 220.

q.t: The largest possible sphere is cut from a cube of side 10 cm. What is volume of sphere : volume of cube?
q.e: The sphere's diameter is the side, so r = 5. (4/3)π × 125 : 1000 = 500π/3 : 1000 = π : 6.

q.t: Four cubes of side 2 cm are joined in a row. How much less surface area does the cuboid have than the four cubes had?
q.e: Each of the 3 joints hides two faces of 4 cm², so 3 × 8 = 24 cm² is lost. Check: 4 × 24 = 96, and the 8 × 2 × 2 cuboid has 2(16 + 16 + 4) = 72.

q.t: A hemisphere of diameter 7 cm is scooped out of one face of a cube of side 10 cm. Find the surface area of what is left. (π = 22/7)
q.e: The flat circle πr² is removed, but the hollow adds 2πr² inside. Net +πr² = 38.5 — the same change as sticking a hemisphere on. 600 + 38.5 = 638.5.

q.t: A glass is a cylinder 10 cm tall with inner diameter 5 cm, but its base is a raised hemisphere of radius 2.5 cm. How much does it really hold? (π = 3.14)
q.e: It looks like πr²h = 3.14 × 6.25 × 10 = 196.25. But the raised hemisphere, (2/3)πr³ ≈ 32.71, takes up space, so it really holds about 196.25 − 32.71 = 163.54.
